images.title: What an *AI Bookkeeper* does, and what it costs
images.sub: Invoices, receivables, bank matching and month-end, split into what an AI Employee owns and what stays with a person.

images.name: duties
images.title: The bookkeeping job, *duty by duty*
rows: Creates invoices from the time tracker, practice system or lease and sends them the day they're due.
Sends reminders before and after the due date in your wording. Payment plan requests go to a person.
Reads each bill, codes it, matches the purchase order and flags duplicates and price jumps.
Matches every bank and card line each morning and splits payouts into sales, fees and refunds.
Reconciles accounts and drafts the reports. A person reviews and closes the month.
Prepares the payment run. A person releases money and confirms any new bank details.

images.name: by-industry
images.title: What it handles, *by industry*
head: Business
The AI Bookkeeper handles
It hands to a person
rows: Patient balances, insurer remittances, supplier bills
Invoices from time entries, reminders, operating account matching
Rent charges, tenant reminders, maintenance bills
Payout splits, fees, refunds, inventory bills
Retainer invoices, contractor bills, card receipts
images.source: Examples. Every business sets its own rules.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A day at a *marketing agency*
rows: Matches 41 new bank and card lines from overnight. Three don't match and go on a question list.
Sends the 30-day reminder on an overdue invoice and resends a copy to a client who says they never got it.
Codes 12 bills from the inbox and catches a contractor invoice sent twice.
A vendor emails new bank details. It holds the change and asks the owner to confirm by phone.
Bills three retainers when the milestones close in the project tracker.
Prepares Thursday's payment run, 9 bills, and sends it to the owner to approve.
Updates the aged receivables list and asks the account lead about a $1,180 card charge.

images.name: setup
images.title: How an AI Bookkeeper *is set up*
steps: Every account, payment processor, bill source and the rules for how each kind of transaction is coded.
Accounting software, bank feeds, payouts and the bills inbox, with only the access the job needs.
What it codes and sends alone, and what waits for a person: payments, bank details, write-offs.
It codes and matches everything while a person checks. Nothing posts until the mistakes stop.
It takes on more as its work holds up, and every change goes into the log.
Someone reads the log and updates it when accounts, clients or software change.
